description: 由自承认技术债务注释直接支持的技术债务机制类别。

children.category: known correctness defect or runtime failure
children.description: Comment asserts existing or generated code yields wrong results, mishandles inputs, loses data, breaks an invariant, or throws an exception, and the author treats the behavior as defective.

children.category: unverified behavior, comprehension, or suspected defect
children.description: Author lacks confirmation about runtime behavior, input acceptance, concurrency, semantics, why code exists, or suspects a specific structural, shape, traversal, numerical, or theoretical problem without asserting a failure symptom; verification or investigation is deferred.

children.category: open design, organizational, or speculative proposal
children.description: Author poses an unresolved design, API, placement, suitability, or feature-adoption question, possibly with a provisional answer or hedge, and does not commit to implementation; alternatives remain pending.

children.category: unimplemented named capability or api-parity gap
children.description: A specific named function, input mode, operator, command, module feature, domain class, distribution step, placeholder, or public symbol is absent or partly implemented, including API-parity gaps; work is additive functionality.

children.category: deferred feature activation or restoration
children.description: An existing capability is present but switched off in an entry point/configuration, or was dropped during migration and should be enabled, restored, or ported back.

children.category: component integration or workflow wiring gap
children.description: Named existing components are not wired into the workflow, pipeline, or architecture; pending work is composition or plumbing, not a new algorithm.

children.category: configuration externalization, parameterization, or argument propagation
children.description: A hard-coded, fixed, computed-in-module, workspace-specific, or magic value/path/param/dtype/threshold should be exposed as configuration, derived, or passed to all sibling calls; includes unresolved configurability gaps.

children.category: redundant or inert parameter or api surface debt
children.description: Overlapping configuration knobs should be consolidated/removed, or a named option/parameter has no effect on behavior and silently misleads; API-surface redundancy or unwired config.

children.category: validation, guard, contract, or diagnostic feedback gap
children.description: Required guards, type/default checks, shape compatibility, invalid layer combinations, argument contracts, or runtime preconditions are absent, undefined, unsafe, or undiagnosed; includes unresolved isinstance-vs-duck-typing validation debates.

children.category: test coverage, compatibility, or tooling infrastructure debt
children.description: Tests are missing, disabled, stubbed, weakly asserting, or failing due to CI/platform/encoding/dependency environment; admitted gap is verification or tooling, not production logic.

children.category: documentation, observability, or reporting gap
children.description: Deferred work is to write docs/docstrings/README/tutorials, explain an opaque parameter, clarify test messages, or add logging, timing, warnings, or reporting output; behavior is not claimed wrong.

children.category: self-labeled hack, shared-state, or coupling smell
children.description: Author labels code a hack/kludge/for-now or mutable shared/global state that should be local, or code that exists solely to satisfy another module's method/flag, admitting hidden coupling.

children.category: test-only scaffolding in production code
children.description: A parameter, constant, or branch exists only to satisfy tests but lives in shipped application code; test concern mixed into production.

children.category: deferred structural refactor, representation, or interface redesign
children.description: Deferred change to data representation, object model, local code shape, public signature/input contract, or abstraction level (dict to tuple, split functions, separate data from metadata, narrow over-general implementation, lighter identifier).

children.category: structural relocation, extraction, duplication, coupling, or canonical migration
children.description: Existing code is misplaced, wrongly partitioned, duplicated, entangled across layers, or bespoke where a library abstraction exists; remedy is move, extract into class/file, consolidate, delete, decouple, or propagate canonical change.

children.category: naming or api-cleanup debt
children.description: Proposed rename of an identifier, parameter, field, or option for consistency, spelling, or convention alignment; primarily nomenclature and public-surface tidiness.

children.category: performance, idiom, or redundant recomputation debt
children.description: Working code is inefficient in time/memory or non-idiomatic, performs redundant recomputation or initialization, or artifact names a faster/cheaper primitive, vectorization, in-place rewrite, lazy loading, or complexity concern.

children.category: external-dependency workaround or cross-file or external-source debt
children.description: Local code compensates for a named third-party/upstream/rendering/library/version constraint or lags external API drift; or debt originates in another file, external repo, or informal source.

children.category: methodological or domain-assumption concern
children.description: Current statistical/algorithmic approach or WIP feature rests on a strong dataset-wide or domain assumption that may not generalize; documented inline without concrete fix.

children.category: alternative algorithm, model, or heuristic quality debt
children.description: Artifact names a specific alternative mathematical formulation/algorithmic option, says a core algorithm or heuristic should be improved, or proposes changing a named model capacity/hyperparameter from a hunch; no failing input recorded.

children.category: device, memory, aliasing, or state-serialization debt
children.description: Code makes a suboptimal hardware/device decision, has aliasing/copy-semantics uncertainty, unresolved reference-count ownership, import-cycle blocker, or fails to pass values/checkpoints across process boundaries.

children.category: packaging, manual-setup, or asset-bundling gap
children.description: A packaging manifest lacks required declarations, a setup/provisioning step is delegated to the user, or generated output depends on external assets/CDNs that should be bundled so output is self-contained.

children.category: behavioral override or normative policy reversal
children.description: Current behavior is too aggressive, strict, or a configuration choice may be wrong; gating/relaxing is proposed, or a normative rule current code should adopt is asserted with relatively strong commitment.

children.category: version- or status-gated removal
children.description: Removal or substitution of code is tied to a release version, API experimental status, or deprecation state; debt is time-bounded or status-bounded with no re-enablement.

children.category: cleanup, dead-code removal, or unscheduled deletion
children.description: Working code should be deleted, de-duplicated locally, renamed locally, or tidied without claiming behavioral fault; removal or cleanup has no version, status, or named replacement trigger.

children.category: personal-state or hand-off deferral
children.description: TODO postpones work by citing author's momentary personal state (sleepiness, lack of time), waiting on a stated precondition, or delegating to another collaborator, without claiming a defect.

children.category: deferred benchmark or parallelism work
children.description: Empirical comparison, measurement, optimization, timing, parallelization, or incremental infrastructure work is outstanding; no correctness problem is alleged.

children.category: enhancement or example-quality desire
children.description: Desirable improvement to working code, examples, or data that is not a defect: better illustrative dataset, optional multi-GPU support, example-quality suggestion.

children.category: formatting, style, readability, or organizational cleanup
children.description: The admitted debt is cosmetic or presentational: formatting/lint conformance, banner or grouping tidiness, or a low-confidence claim that code is hard to read, misnamed stylistically, or "could be smarter" without naming a speed, correctness or structural mechanism.

children.category: bare or underspecified deferred marker
children.description: TODO has only a marker, author tag, lone noun/symbol/fragment, pronoun, truncated fragment, generic phrase, or self-doubting note with no reconstructable action or target; only debt location is inferable.
